UNIT 1 — Weather and Moon Phases
S4E4, S4E2  │  Aug 10 – Sept 4, 2026  │  18 instructional days
	 
STAGE 1: DESIRED RESULTS
	ESTABLISHED GOALS
Standards: S4E4. Obtain, evaluate, and communicate information to identify weather patterns and phenomena. S4E2. Obtain, evaluate, and communicate information to model the effects of the position and motion of the Earth and the moon in relation to the sun.
Vocabulary: weather, climate, temperature, precipitation, meteorologist, moon phase, lunar cycle, waxing, waning
	TRANSFER
Students will independently use their learning to…
Students will independently collect and analyze weather and moon-phase data to identify patterns and make predictions about future conditions.
	UNDERSTANDING
Students will understand that…
•  Weather changes can be observed, measured, and recorded to identify patterns over time.
•  The moon moves through a predictable, repeating cycle of phases.
•  Scientists use data and instruments to describe and forecast weather and climate.
	ESSENTIAL QUESTIONS
Students will keep considering…
•  How can we use data to identify patterns in weather over time?
•  Why does the moon appear to change shape throughout the month?
•  How is climate different from weather?
	ACQUISITION — Students will KNOW…
How to collect and record weather data (temperature, precipitation, cloud cover); the sequence of moon phases; the difference between weather and climate.
	ACQUISITION — Students will be SKILLED AT…
Collecting, recording, and analyzing weather and moon-phase data; identifying patterns and explaining changes over time using evidence.
	 
STAGE 2: EVIDENCE
	LEARNING TARGET
	ASSESSMENT
	I can: collect, record, and analyze weather data to identify patterns.
	Standard: S4E4.a, S4E4.c
	I can: describe and sequence the phases of the moon.
	Standard: S4E2.b
	I can: explain how weather and moon-phase data changes over time.
	Standard: S4E4.a, S4E2.b
	RUBRIC OVERVIEW
Students can demonstrate mastery of S4E4, S4E2 through STEMscopes investigations, GaDOE Inspire phenomenon tasks, and the Unit 1 Assessment.
DOK Level 4 — Distinguished  │  DOK Level 3 — Proficient  │  DOK Level 2 — Developing  │  DOK Level 1 — Beginning
	 
UNIT 2 — Stars, Planets, and Moon
S4E1, S4E2, S4P1.c  │  Sept 7 – Oct 30, 2026  │  34 instructional days
	 
STAGE 1: DESIRED RESULTS
	ESTABLISHED GOALS
Standards: S4E1. Obtain, evaluate, and communicate information to compare and contrast the physical attributes of stars and planets. S4E2. Obtain, evaluate, and communicate information to model the effects of the position and motion of the Earth and the moon in relation to the sun. S4P1.c. Model how light travels and interacts with objects (reflection/refraction).
Vocabulary: star, planet, solar system, orbit, rotation, revolution, axis, season, reflection, refraction
	TRANSFER
Students will independently use their learning to…
Students will independently use models and evidence to explain the motion of the Earth, moon, and sun, and to compare objects in our solar system.
	UNDERSTANDING
Students will understand that…
•  Stars and planets have distinct physical attributes that can be compared using evidence and technology.
•  The Earth's rotation and revolution, and the moon's orbit, explain day/night, seasons, and moon phases.
•  Light travels in predictable ways and can be reflected or refracted by objects.
	ESSENTIAL QUESTIONS
Students will keep considering…
•  How are stars and planets similar and different?
•  Why do we experience seasons, day and night, and changing moon phases?
•  How does light behave when it interacts with different objects?
	ACQUISITION — Students will KNOW…
The physical attributes that distinguish stars from planets; how the Earth's rotation and revolution and the moon's orbit cause observable patterns; how light reflects and refracts.
	ACQUISITION — Students will be SKILLED AT…
Using models to explain Earth-sun-moon relationships; comparing stars and planets using evidence; investigating reflection and refraction of light.
	 
STAGE 2: EVIDENCE
	LEARNING TARGET
	ASSESSMENT
	I can: compare stars and planets using evidence and technology.
	Standard: S4E1
	I can: create and use models to explain seasons, day/night, and moon phases.
	Standard: S4E2
	I can: investigate and explain how light reflects and refracts.
	Standard: S4P1.c
	RUBRIC OVERVIEW
Students can demonstrate mastery of S4E1, S4E2, S4P1.c through STEMscopes investigations, GaDOE Inspire phenomenon tasks, and the Unit 2 Assessment.

	TRANSFER

Vocabulary: producer, consumer, decomposer, food chain, food web, ecosystem, energy flow, community
	TRANSFER
Students will independently use their learning to…
Students will independently construct food chains/webs and explain how changes in an ecosystem affect the flow of energy to living things.
	UNDERSTANDING
Students will understand that…
•  All organisms in an ecosystem play a role — producer, consumer, or decomposer — in the flow of energy.

	ESSENTIAL QUESTIONS

•  What happens to an ecosystem when one part of it changes?
•  How are producers, consumers, and decomposers connected?

The roles of producers, consumers, and decomposers; how to construct and interpret food chains and food webs.
	ACQUISITION — Students will be SKILLED AT…

•  How does gravity affect the motion of objects?

The difference between balanced and unbalanced forces; how gravity affects motion; the six types of simple machines and their uses.

UNIT 1 — Weather and Moon Phases
S4E4, S4E2  │  Aug 10 – Sept 4, 2026  │  18 instructional days
	 
STAGE 1: DESIRED RESULTS
	ESTABLISHED GOALS
Standards: S4E4. Obtain, evaluate, and communicate information to identify weather patterns and phenomena. S4E2. Obtain, evaluate, and communicate information to model the effects of the position and motion of the Earth and the moon in relation to the sun.
Vocabulary: weather, climate, temperature, precipitation, meteorologist, moon phase, lunar cycle, waxing, waning
	TRANSFER
Students will independently use their learning to…
Students will independently collect and analyze weather and moon-phase data to identify patterns and make predictions about future conditions.
	UNDERSTANDING
Students will understand that…
•  Weather changes can be observed, measured, and recorded to identify patterns over time.
•  The moon moves through a predictable, repeating cycle of phases.
•  Scientists use data and instruments to describe and forecast weather and climate.
	ESSENTIAL QUESTIONS
Students will keep considering…
•  How can we use data to identify patterns in weather over time?
•  Why does the moon appear to change shape throughout the month?
•  How is climate different from weather?
	ACQUISITION — Students will KNOW…
How to collect and record weather data (temperature, precipitation, cloud cover); the sequence of moon phases; the difference between weather and climate.
	ACQUISITION — Students will be SKILLED AT…
Collecting, recording, and analyzing weather and moon-phase data; identifying patterns and explaining changes over time using evidence.
	 
STAGE 2: EVIDENCE
	LEARNING TARGET
	ASSESSMENT
	I can: collect, record, and analyze weather data to identify patterns.
	Standard: S4E4.a, S4E4.c
	I can: describe and sequence the phases of the moon.
	Standard: S4E2.b
	I can: explain how weather and moon-phase data changes over time.
	Standard: S4E4.a, S4E2.b
	RUBRIC OVERVIEW
Students can demonstrate mastery of S4E4, S4E2 through STEMscopes investigations, GaDOE Inspire phenomenon tasks, and the Unit 1 Assessment.

S4E1, S4E2, S4P1.c  │  Sept 7 – Oct 30, 2026  │  34 instructional days
	 
STAGE 1: DESIRED RESULTS
	ESTABLISHED GOALS
Standards: S4E1. Obtain, evaluate, and communicate information to compare and contrast the physical attributes of stars and planets. S4E2. Obtain, evaluate, and communicate information to model the effects of the position and motion of the Earth and the moon in relation to the sun. S4P1.c. Model how light travels and interacts with objects (reflection/refraction).
Vocabulary: star, planet, solar system, orbit, rotation, revolution, axis, season, reflection, refraction
	TRANSFER
Students will independently use their learning to…
Students will independently use models and evidence to explain the motion of the Earth, moon, and sun, and to compare objects in our solar system.
	UNDERSTANDING
Students will understand that…
•  Stars and planets have distinct physical attributes that can be compared using evidence and technology.
•  The Earth's rotation and revolution, and the moon's orbit, explain day/night, seasons, and moon phases.
•  Light travels in predictable ways and can be reflected or refracted by objects.
	ESSENTIAL QUESTIONS
Students will keep considering…
•  How are stars and planets similar and different?
•  Why do we experience seasons, day and night, and changing moon phases?
•  How does light behave when it interacts with different objects?
	ACQUISITION — Students will KNOW…
The physical attributes that distinguish stars from planets; how the Earth's rotation and revolution and the moon's orbit cause observable patterns; how light reflects and refracts.
	ACQUISITION — Students will be SKILLED AT…
Using models to explain Earth-sun-moon relationships; comparing stars and planets using evidence; investigating reflection and refraction of light.

•  How do meteorologists use evidence to forecast the weather?

	ESTABLISHED GOALS
Standards: S4L1. Obtain, evaluate, and communicate information about the roles of organisms and the flow of energy within an ecosystem.
Vocabulary: producer, consumer, decomposer, food chain, food web, ecosystem, energy flow, community
	TRANSFER
Students will independently use their learning to…
Students will independently construct food chains/webs and explain how changes in an ecosystem affect the flow of energy to living things.
	UNDERSTANDING
Students will understand that…
•  All organisms in an ecosystem play a role — producer, consumer, or decomposer — in the flow of energy.
•  Energy flows from the sun through producers to consumers and decomposers in a food chain or web.
•  Changes in an ecosystem affect the organisms living within it.
	ESSENTIAL QUESTIONS
Students will keep considering…
•  How does energy flow through an ecosystem?
•  What happens to an ecosystem when one part of it changes?
•  How are producers, consumers, and decomposers connected?
	ACQUISITION — Students will KNOW…
The roles of producers, consumers, and decomposers; how to construct and interpret food chains and food webs.
	ACQUISITION — Students will be SKILLED AT…
Creating food chains and webs; identifying producers, consumers, and decomposers; explaining how ecosystem changes affect energy flow.

STAGE 1: DESIRED RESULTS
	ESTABLISHED GOALS
Standards: S4P3. Obtain, evaluate, and communicate information about the relationship between balanced and unbalanced forces.
Vocabulary: force, motion, balanced force, unbalanced force, gravity, simple machine, lever, pulley, inclined plane
	TRANSFER
Students will independently use their learning to…
Students will independently plan and carry out investigations to explain how balanced and unbalanced forces, including gravity, affect the motion of objects, and how simple machines change the force needed to complete a task.
	UNDERSTANDING
Students will understand that…
•  Balanced forces do not change an object's motion; unbalanced forces cause a change in speed or direction.
•  Gravity is a force that pulls objects toward the Earth and affects their motion.
•  Simple machines change the amount of force needed to do work.
	ESSENTIAL QUESTIONS
Students will keep considering…
•  What happens to an object's motion when forces acting on it are balanced or unbalanced?
•  How does gravity affect the motion of objects?
•  How do simple machines make work easier?
	ACQUISITION — Students will KNOW…
The difference between balanced and unbalanced forces; how gravity affects motion; the six types of simple machines and their uses.
	ACQUISITION — Students will be SKILLED AT…
Planning and carrying out investigations on balanced/unbalanced forces; constructing arguments about gravity's effect on motion; explaining how simple machines change force.
	 
STAGE 2: EVIDENCE
	LEARNING TARGET
	ASSESSMENT
	I can: plan and carry out an investigation on the effects of balanced and unbalanced forces on an object.
	Standard: S4P3.a
	I can: construct an argument that gravitational force affects the motion of an object.
	Standard: S4P3.b
	I can: explain the uses of simple machines and how they change force.
